title: Never-assertions under early stopping hold in every run taken
situation: 0088 stops a batch at four passes; the examples say a never-assertion holds in all 5 runs. The lead asked which governs. It also asked whether held-out agents 4, which failed in judgment and which the lead has now seen, is re-run or replaced.
decision: A never-assertion must hold in every run a batch takes: the batch passes at four passing runs only if no run it took violated one, and fails on the first violation in any run; 'all 5' in the examples means every run taken. Held-out agents 4 is re-run, not replaced: it is revealed to the lead, whose role in judgment is to see it, but not to the builders, who learn only the concept and the shortfall; a held-out case is replaced only once a builder has seen it.
consequences: The examples' run rule is read this way in every cut; no example text changes.
